![Regeneration basal area 10 years after harvest by retained-overstory treatment. Points are arithmetic expected basal area, including modeled zeros and integrated over fitted site and nested macro-plot random intercepts; colored ranges are 95% confidence intervals for the means from the full-parameter log-scale delta method. Blue ranges with circles denote redwood and orange ranges with triangles denote tanoak. Each species is modeled separately using zero-inflated Gamma responses with treatment as a fixed effect and four site and 16 nested macro-plot random intercepts, using 64 vegetation-plot observations per species. Redwood zero probability varies by treatment; tanoak zero probability is constant. The zero components have no random effects. GS = group selection; LD = low-density dispersed retention; HA = high-density aggregated retention; HD = high-density dispersed retention. Species panels use different vertical scales. Intervals describe uncertainty in means, not new-plot variation or pairwise significance tests.](/outputs/regeneration/selected-species-models/figures/rd02-selected-species-basal-area.png){#fig-rd02-regeneration-basal-area width="100%" fig-alt="Redwood and tanoak mean regeneration basal area with 95% confidence intervals for GS, LD, HA, and HD retention treatments in two species panels. Redwood means are highest in GS and lowest in HD, with wide uncertainty in GS. Tanoak means vary less across treatments."}
